text: Because trajectory error grows exponentially, the predictability horizon grows only logarithmically with measurement precision, so improving precision by a factor of 10 adds only about one Lyapunov time of forecast.
explanation: With error ~ e^{lambda t}, the horizon T ~ (1/lambda) ln(delta/epsilon) grows logarithmically in precision, so a 10x better measurement buys only ln(10)/lambda, roughly one extra Lyapunov time. The statement is true.
